description: Verification scenarios for Telltale Legacy. Every claim in the docs must map to a scenario here, and every scenario declares whether a machine check or a human at the keyboard produced the evidence. This keeps automated checks from being read as proof of gameplay behaviour.

modes.automated: Reproducible without the game running; the harness or a tool asserts the outcome.
modes.manual-attended: A person plays the game; the agent may only observe, capture evidence and record results.

scenarios.asserts: File count, hashes, PE sections including .bind, ttarch versions and content groups.
Build identity, archive version, required runtime and save-dir writability; fails closed.
Hash-verified backup, byte-identical restore, tamper rejection, pre-restore preservation.
Magic and declared-size fields parse, magic is recognised, truncated input does not crash, output never lands in the save root.
A save set is reported identical across a restart, and a rewritten prefs.prop is detected.
Every profile episode directory exists with at least one archive, so no episode is silently absent.
The marked hosts block parses correctly and no game socket reaches a remote endpoint while blocked.
Episode 1 reaches the main menu with the publisher API unreachable.
A new game is started and the game writes save_N.save plus prefs.prop while the API is unreachable.
After a clean exit and relaunch with the API unreachable, the slot list appears and CONTINUE resumes the saved checkpoint.
Decisions made before saving remain in effect after the reload.
scenarios.note: Progression across a checkpoint is verified behaviourally. The container is opaque, so the encoded decision values themselves cannot be read back.

scenarios.asserts: Completing Episode 1 advances to Episode 2 with the API unreachable.
scenarios.note: Requires a full Episode 1 playthrough; packs 102-105 are verified present but the transition itself has not been played.
Content is not installed: only WalkingDead106 backpatch overlays exist in the five episode packs.
